name: Business Owner Work and Residency Permit

requirements.blocker_text: Must register a business in Lebanon (via the Investment Development Authority of Lebanon's business-registration process), then apply for prior approval to practice a profession from the Ministry of Labour, through a Lebanese mission abroad or an authorized representative.
requirements.fix_path: Register the business with IDAL, then file the Ministry of Labour work-authorization application.

outcome.duration_length: not confirmed precisely in this build; described as renewable

sources.title: Investment Development Authority of Lebanon (IDAL) -- government investment-promotion agency's FAQ confirming a foreign investor/business owner applies for Ministry of Labour work authorization (via a Lebanese mission abroad or authorized representative), with IDAL's Business Support Unit able to facilitate the licensing process

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Lebanon). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- sourced to IDAL, Lebanon's own government investment authority, tier 1. GENUINE FINDING, NOT A GAP: no minimum investment or capital threshold was specified anywhere in IDAL's own FAQ content reviewed in this build -- consistent with the same no-minimum-threshold pattern found in this dataset for Tunisia's Investment Law and Iran's FIPPA license; the gate here is Ministry of Labour discretionary work-authorization approval, not a numeric floor. SEPARATE, RELATED FINDING NOT MODELED AS PART OF THIS ROUTE: IDAL's own legal-framework document on land ownership confirms foreign nationals may own up to 3,000 square meters of land/built property without prior authorization (subject to aggregate 3% national / 3% per-Caza / 10% Beirut caps), with Council of Ministers decree approval required above that threshold -- but the same document does not state that property ownership itself grants or leads to a residency permit, so real-estate ownership has deliberately NOT been modeled as this route's qualifying mechanism to avoid asserting a link the source doesn't support. family_can_join set false (not asserted true without a source) and family_can_work left null since dependents' rights under this specific business-owner permit were not detailed in the source reviewed.
